 Appealing an IRMAA Determination Resulting in a Higher Medicare Part B Premium
 By Ed Zurndorfer 10/25/2026 FEDVIP coverage FEHB premiums FSAFEDS updates Open Season 2027 PSHB changes 
 The Federal Benefits Open Season for the 2027 plan year will be held from November 9 through December 14, 2026. During the Federal Benefits Open Season (referred to as “open season), Federal and Postal Service employees can enroll, change or cancel participation in the:
 Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) program for Federal employees and retirees.
 Postal Service Health Benefit (PSHB) program for Postal Service employees and retirees.
 Federal Employees Dental and Vision Program (FEDVIP) for employees and retirees, and
 Federal Flexible Spending Account Program (FSAFEDS) for active employees only.
 This is the first of a series of FEDZONE columns presenting information about the four programs. The information presented will hopefully assist employees and retirees make informed decisions with respect to their and their family’s health, dental and vision insurance coverages during 2027.
 Federal employees and retirees should be aware that their current health insurance, dental and vision insurance enrollment automatically continues from the current plan year  to the next plan year unless a participant chooses to make a change during Open Season. However, current FSAFEDS enrollment requires re-enrollment each year for employees who wish to continue participating in the next plan year.
 New for 2027 
 As has been true in past years, Federal and Postal Service employees are encouraged to consider the tax savings available through FSAFEDS. Setting aside an annual amount deducted from their gross salary that an employee projects to spend on out-of-pocket for health care, dental and vision care, and dependent care via a flexible spending account (FSA) result in federal and state tax savings for FSAFEDS participants.   For 2027, a new item is the addition of the FSAFEDS  VISA FSA card for HCFSA and LEX HCFSA accounts. FSAFEDS participants will have the choice of using a debit card or paperless reimbursement.
 FEHB program for family eligibility. The FEHB Protection Act of 2025 requires OPM to strengthen family member eligibility verification and oversight within the FEHB program. Beginning with this year’s 2026 “open season”, any Federal or Postal Service employee or retiree who is adding a new family member to their FEHB program or PSHB health plan program during “open season” must submit supporting documentation to obtain verification of the family member’s eligibility.
 Federal government share of premiums and cost trends for 2027 
 The federal government’s share of premiums paid for the FEHB program is set by law. It is known as the “Fair Share” formula and is designed to maintain a consistent level of government contributions as a percentage of total program costs. This is regardless of which health insurance plan or type of enrollment (self, self plus one or self and family) an employee or a retiree elects.
 The federal government contribution is calculated separately for the FEHB program and the PSHB program. For most employees and retirees, the federal government contribution equals the lesser of: (1) 72 percent of the amounts OPM determines are the program-wide weighted average of premiums in effect each year for self only, self plus one, and self and family enrollments, respectively; or (2) 75 percent of the total premium for the particular plan an enrollee selects.
 For FEHB program health plans in 2027:
 Overall average premium increase: 9.3 percent, down from 10.2 percent in 2026.
 Average enrollee share increase: 10.9 percent, down from 12.3 percent in 2026; and
 Federal government share increase: 8.6 percent, down from 9.2 percent in 2026.
 For PSHB program health plans in 2027:
 Overall average premium increase: 6.7 percent, down from 9 percent in 2026.
 Average enrollee share increase: 8.2 percent, down from 11.3 percent in 2026; and
 Federal government contribution increase: 6.0 percent, down from 8.0 percent in 2026.
 FEHB program and PSHB program premium increases are being driven primarily by: (1) Rising prices and utilization across inpatient, physician, outpatient and surgical services; (2) Continued growth in behavioral and metal health care; and (3) Higher prescription drug spending, in particular on GLF-1 drugs, specialty drugs and other high-cost therapies.
 2027 health insurance premium rate charts showing the actual premium rate adjustment for each FEHB program health plan and enrollment type may be viewed at:
 https://www.opm.gov/healthcare-insurance/healthcare/plan-information/premiums 
 PSHB eligible members seeking PSHB health plan information should go to:
         https://www.opm.gov/healthcare-insurance/pshb/premiums 
 All prospective and current Federal and Postal Service employees are encouraged to carefully review plan-specific premium changes. They are advised that premiums are just one factor to consider when choosing a health insurance plan. In addition, employees are advised to evaluate health plan quality and coverage information in order to make the best decision for themselves and their families.
